rules.title: Fair housing discrimination restrictions in Cambridge housing transactions
rules.requirement: Landlords, sellers, and rental agents in Cambridge may not discriminate in rental housing transactions or tenancy terms based on protected categories such as disability, race, national origin, family status, source of income, marital status, sex, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, age, religion, military status, relationship status, or family structure. Tenant selection standards must be reasonable and applied equally and uniformly to all applicants.

coverage.summary: Applies to Cambridge housing discrimination in real estate transactions, including viewing or renting an apartment and tenancy terms, with an exemption noted for owner-occupied 2-family dwellings.

rules.exemptions: The document states: “there is an exemption for 2-family dwellings, when the owner lives there.”
rules.penalty: The Commission may provide remedies including filing a criminal complaint in District Court, civil fines of up to $300 for each violation, filing a civil complaint in Superior Court seeking injunctive relief, and seeking damages, expenses and other relief.
rules.interaction: The document states the Cambridge Human Rights Commission enforces the Cambridge Fair Housing Ordinance and that either party may remove certain Fair Housing Ordinance cases to Massachusetts Superior Court or the Attorney General’s Office.
rules.quoted_span: Under the law, landlords, sellers and rental agents may use any reasonable standard to determine which applicants are selected, as long as that standard is applied equally and uniformly to all applicants.
